newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - Stora signals no forestry pickup.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Stora signals no forestry pickup.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Stora AB on Thursday posted an expected sharp drop in profits for the first nine months of 1996 and gave analysts no hope of any short-term pick-up in the forestry sector.

Stora said pulp operations were hit by slack demand and weak price levels in the nine months to September 30, prompting a sharp fall in profit after financial items to 1.92 billion crowns ($292 million) from 6.19 billion a year ago.

The company's managing director Lars-Ake Helgesson told a press conference that 1996 was an interim year for Stora, which struggled to regain its footing after the forestry sector began to take a beating in late 1995.
"We are still expecting a difficult year in 1997 but it is reasonable to expect the business cycle will be better than in 1996," said Helgesson.
Analysts said the result was as expected, with a market consensus of 1.89 billion crowns for profit after financial items.
However the technical paper unit and packaging divisions were picked out as faring slightly worse than expected while some analysts said newsprint was in better shape.
"It was in line with expectations but I can't see Stora making much money next quarter," analyst Mads Asprem of Morgan Stanley said.
"It is hard to say what will happen in 1997 but I think we will start the year at the same levels as now."
Other analysts were also gloomy about the fourth quarter of 1996 after sales in the nine months slumped to 34.25 billion crowns from 43.26 billion a year ago.

"Volumes should be higher in the fourth quarter but prices for newsprint, SC (uncoated) paper and LWC (coated magazine) paper will be lower on average while fine paper prices should be higher," said Thomas Brodin, Salomon Brothers's European pulp and paper analyst.
Brodin said there was little to look forward to in 1997.
"I think Stora's earnings will go down next year," he said.
Stora said the fall in profits in the first nine months was due to delivery volumes falling eight percent, coupled with a deterioration in prices for virtually all products.
Operating income slumped to 2.32 billion crowns from 6.98 billion a year earlier.
"Translated into Swedish crowns, average prices for Stora's pulp, paper and board products were 16 percent lower (than a year ago)," Stora said in a statement.
"In addition, the strengthened crown had an adverse effect on invoicing in an amount of 2.5 billion crowns."
Stora said a weak economic trend in Europe affected markets for paper and board although demand in the U.S. was slightly better but deliveries were lower than a year ago.

Prices for pulp, LWC, fine papers and board fell in the first half of the year due to the weak market. Prices for paper pulp increased in the third quarter. Fine paper prices were raised in September by about 10 percent in all European markets. ($1=6.570 Swedish Crown)
